cole.name: Gerrit Cole
cole.summary: CV model picks slider/sweeper vs four-seam from glove presentation and facial set timing.

tips.title: Glove flare → slider family
tips.lookFor: With a runner on first in the stretch, watch his glove in the half-second before hand break: if it flares open wider off his belt line, the pitch is usually a slider or sweeper—not a four-seam.

tips.title: Early cheek freeze → four-seam
tips.lookFor: From hitter view with bases empty, if his cheek/jaw set locks still earlier in the windup, expect four-seam. Later or softer facial set more often precedes offspeed.

rodon.name: Carlos Rodón
rodon.summary: CV model separates changeup from four-seam on PitchCom tap pattern and plant-foot width in stretch.

tips.title: PitchCom taps → changeup vs FF
tips.lookFor: With a runner on second, count the glove-side taps before he separates: two short taps usually mean changeup; one longer hold usually means four-seam.

tips.title: Wide plant → sinker
tips.lookFor: From the first-base camera in stretch, if his lead foot plants wider relative to the rubber edge, look sinker. Narrower plant more often precedes other pitch types.

yamamoto.name: Yoshinobu Yamamoto
yamamoto.summary: Highest-confidence CV picks: grip peek separates splitter from four-seam; glove height at set separates breaking ball from FF.

tips.title: Grip peek → splitter vs FF
tips.lookFor: In windup from the third-base side, watch for a brief finger silhouette over the glove rim: a visible split gap usually means splitter; a closed look usually means four-seam.

tips.title: High glove at set → breaker
tips.lookFor: In stretch with first occupied, if his glove sits clearly above the belt at set, expect curve or slider. Glove parked at the belt more often means four-seam.

glasnow.name: Tyler Glasnow
glasnow.summary: CV model uses windup hand-path length to separate curve from four-seam before release.

tips.title: Long backswing → curve
tips.lookFor: With bases empty, compare the length of his hand path before glove break: a longer backswing arc usually means curveball; a shorter path usually means four-seam.
